figures.finding: The Netherlands Antilles ceased to exist as a country on 10 October 2010, when the amended Charter for the Kingdom entered into force: Curaçao and St Maarten became countries within the Kingdom, and Bonaire, St Eustatius and Saba became public bodies of the Netherlands. A life placed there after that date follows CW, SX or BQ; before it, the Antillean rules below.

sources.said: It was decided that the amended Charter for the Kingdom of the Netherlands would enter into force on 10 October 2010. Since that date, the Netherlands Antilles has ceased to exist as a country.
Under the new structure, Curaçao and St Maarten have acquired the status of countries within the Kingdom, similar to Aruba

figures.finding: The Netherlands Antilles' Labour Regulations 2000 (art. 15) ban child labour for children of fourteen and under (children being those under fifteen), but let children do light work typical of children (delivering newspapers, packing groceries) outside school hours and not before 07:00 or after 19:00; the Youth Employment Decree bars harmful work below sixteen, with written exemptions from the Director of the Labour Affairs Department; young people of 15 to 18 are barred from night and hazardous work.

value.exemption: written application to the Director of the Labour Affairs Department

figures.applies: Netherlands Antilles; the Kingdom's 2006 report on the Antillean rules.

sources.said: Article 15 of the Labour Regulations specifies that this ban applies to children aged 14 and under.
They may not, however, do this kind of work during school hours, or before 07.00 or after 19.00.
Should an employer wish to do so, he must apply in writing to the Director of the Labour Affairs Department.

figures.finding: The age of majority in the Netherlands Antilles was 21 under the old Civil Code and became 18 under article 233 of the new Civil Code (NBWNA), whose Book 1 came into force on 15 January 2001; a minor also comes of age by marriage, and an unmarried mother of 16 may be declared of age.

value.law: Nieuw Burgerlijk Wetboek van de Nederlandse Antillen, Boek 1, art. 233

figures.applies: Netherlands Antilles, 15 January 2001 to 10 October 2010 (21 before 2001).

sources.said: Majority is attained when a child reaches a certain age (currently 21, but this has been lowered to 18 in the NBWNA; upon marriage; or, the case of unmarried mothers, through a declaration of majority (art. 233 NBWNA) when they reach the age of 16.
The NBW Book 1 came into force on 15 January 2001
